observations: Reachable ancestry is a conditional positive witness for ordinary descendant overwrite: if the stable effect identity remains in an ancestor reachable from the inspected ref, a prior commit occurred.
Absence from reachable ancestry is not proof of never-commit because force-rewrite/ref deletion can remove the committing object from the reachable graph.
Once all retaining refs are lost, reachable-history inspection shares the same authority/durability domain as the state it is trying to audit; GC may erase the differentiating object.
Therefore the mechanism cannot universally disambiguate never-committed versus commit-then-overwritten under the required rewrite/GC threat model without an independently surviving witness.
inference: This leaf refines, but does not extend beyond, the already retained authority-domain / reachable-copy / fail-closed GC-boundary mechanism family. It adds the exact conditional statement that reachable ancestry can prove prior commit only while the committing ancestor remains reachable; the negative case remains unresolved and cannot count as exactly-once or Phase-1 closure evidence.
blocker: No independently surviving durability witness exists in this tested leaf; reachable ancestry and current target can both lose differentiating history after rewrite/ref loss/GC.
